questions.question: Which language should the frontend use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed React development with stronger maintainability and safer catalogue data models.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Standard React development without static type checking.

questions.rationale: React/Vite is requested and TypeScript is the recommended default for a product catalogue with exact pricing and subsidy values.

questions.question: Which frontend framework and build approach should be used?

options.label: React + Vite
options.description: Fast client-side React application with Vite development and production builds.

questions.rationale: The requested implementation is explicitly a new React/Vite website.

questions.question: What must the website include?
questions.answer: Create a responsive catalogue for Jai Kisan Engineering Works, an agricultural implements and farm machinery shop, using exactly the 27 products and exact prices/subsidy values supplied in the conversation. Include catalogue filters, search, sorting, product detail modal, subsidy table, contact and WhatsApp actions, accessibility, SEO, and no fake content. Treat the supplied specification as authoritative and do not invent products, prices, subsidy values, claims, testimonials, or other catalogue content.
questions.rationale: The user provided the complete product and experience specification and explicitly requires it to be authoritative.

sharedQuestions.question: Which data stores are required?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use the authoritative catalogue data bundled with the frontend; no server-side persistence is needed.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational database for server-managed catalogue or enquiry data.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Object storage for uploaded or managed media assets.

sharedQuestions.rationale: The requested site is a static React/Vite catalogue with no requested accounts, content management, submissions backend, or persistence.

sharedQuestions.question: Do users need to sign in to access application API features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require users to sign in before accessing application API features.

options.label: No
options.description: Keep the public catalogue and contact actions available without sign-in.

sharedQuestions.rationale: The requested public shop catalogue does not include authenticated application API features.
